resources.string: File scanning uses a signed threat database. Updates are accepted only after cryptographic verification.
Choose a file to start scanning.

The SHA-256 fingerprint matches a known signature in the active database.
This is the standard harmless anti-malware test signature.
The file could not be scanned.
Files and installed-app scan data stay on the device. Internet access is used only for signed threat-database updates.
Threat database is up to date.
Update rejected: digital signature verification failed.
Update rejected: the database package is invalid.
Could not reach the update server.
A clean result only means no known signature was found. It is not a guarantee that a file is safe.
Review user-installed apps using local threat signatures, requested permissions, install source, accessibility services, and package fingerprints.

To perform this security scan, Aman Security reads the installed app list, requested permissions, install source, accessibility-service declarations, and local package fingerprints. This information stays on this device and is not uploaded.
Run a scan to review user-installed apps.
Scanned: %1$s • Needs review: %2$s • High-risk indicators: %3$s • Known threats: %4$s
Installed-app scan could not be completed.
No elevated indicators were found in the user-installed apps scanned.
Permission and behavior indicators provide security context; by themselves they do not prove that an app is malicious.
Installed outside a recognized app store or source could not be verified
No elevated permission or install-source indicators.

Aman will encrypt the selected file inside private app storage, verify its SHA-256 again, and remove the original only if the provider allows deletion. If removal is not possible, quarantine is cancelled.
The file changed after the scan. It was not quarantined. Scan it again before taking action.
The encrypted copy was discarded because the original file could not be removed. The file remains in its original location.
Quarantine could not be completed. The original file was not intentionally removed.
Quarantined files are encrypted with a device-protected key and kept in private app storage. Restore or permanently delete them only when you choose.
Restoring makes the file accessible outside quarantine again. Choose a destination only if you understand the original detection.
The file was restored and removed from quarantine.
Restore was stopped because the restored data did not match the stored SHA-256. The quarantined copy was kept.
The file could not be restored. The quarantined copy was kept.
This removes the encrypted quarantined copy and cannot be undone.
The quarantined file was deleted permanently.
The quarantined file could not be deleted.
Exclusions apply only to the exact SHA-256 you approve. A matching known-threat result is still shown; the exclusion only suppresses the quarantine recommendation for that exact hash.
Add this exact hash to exclusions?
Use exclusions only for files you trust. Aman will continue to display the underlying detection, but will not recommend quarantine for this exact SHA-256 until you remove the exclusion.
The exact file hash was added to exclusions.
A bounded local history of file scan results. It stays on this device and can be cleared at any time.
This removes saved scan-history records. It does not delete quarantined files or exclusions.
